definition: An ensemble learning method that combines predictions from many decision trees, each trained on a random subset of data and features.
details: Random forests reduce overfitting relative to individual decision trees by averaging predictions across many diverse trees, improving generalization and robustness.

explainer.lead: Random Forest is an ensemble learning method combining predictions from many decision trees, each trained on a random subset of data and features. It matters because averaging diverse trees improves generalization and robustness.

tiers.eli5: Ask a hundred people who each saw a different random slice of the problem, then go with the majority answer. One person may be wrong, but the crowd tends to be right.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train many trees each on a random subset of data and features, then average their predictions. Its purpose is reducing overfitting relative to a single decision tree.
tiers.paperLevel: An ensemble learning method that combines predictions from many decision trees, each trained on a random subset of data and features; averaging across diverse trees reduces overfitting and improves generalization and robustness.

explainer.example: On a classification task, each tree sees a random data and feature subset; the forest averages the trees' predictions to produce a more robust output than any single tree.
